claims.text: Spark plasma sintering can enable large-scale reactive synthesis of Cu-containing refractory high-entropy-alloy composites.
SPS provides rapid heating and short sintering durations.
Rapid heating and short sintering durations mitigate incompatibility arising from positive heats of mixing between Cu and refractory elements.
SPS processing of refractory-element and copper powder mixtures forms a fine, uniform dispersion of phases.
SPS limits the growth of unwanted intermetallic compounds in these mixtures.
Rapid consolidation by SPS reduces the time available for phase separation driven by positive mixing enthalpies.
Suppressing phase separation through rapid SPS consolidation fosters a stable microstructure.
SPS produces a dense Cu-containing refractory-alloy composite.
The SPS-processed composite has greater microstructural uniformity than a conventionally sintered composite.
The SPS-processed composite has improved mechanical properties relative to a conventionally sintered composite.
Conventional sintering typically causes greater grain growth because of longer high-temperature exposure.
Conventional sintering typically produces a less uniform phase distribution than SPS.
Changes in alloy composition can alter the predicted SPS outcome.
Poorly controlled thermal gradients during SPS can alter or impair the predicted outcome.
Industrial-scale SPS may present challenges that are absent from laboratory-scale processing.
